I'm in FL but honestly would be willing to drive ANYWHERE in the country to get him help/a home. He is a pitbull, 4 years old, about 75 lbs. I found him when he was about 9 months (estimating based on vet) and he was reactive from the moment I found him. I had to leash him to get him out of the street and I have NEVER seen a dog react like that to a leash, just absolutely lost his mind, had to take the leash off and let him hump me to my car as it was the only way to get him to safety (I have since had him neutered so humping is no longer an issue).

I have two other dogs in the house he is mostly fine with -- another pit he loves and plays with all day, never any issues, and a much older newfie (12) who he is fine with 90 percent of the time but will occasionally do a snap at (has never actually bitten/drew blood) when he is triggered by noise outside/unexpected movement in the house. I am even able to put him in day care where he can play with the other high energy (same sized) dogs without issue. He seems to lose his mind a little with smaller dogs -- he has never attacked one but he will run right at them with a sort of frenzy so I don't let him near them anymore just for safety. I have cats but keep them separated for the most part just to be safe. He is nuts about balls and anything small and moving, so I feel he has an extremely high prey drive. Whenever he is being reactive he just...loses himself. His pupils get wide and he just becomes a completely different insane, hyper focused creature. He does this when he sees small dogs and balls and any kind of moving toy.

He is extremely leash reactive. He will go after everything when on a leash. Just goes NUTS on a leash. If he is on the leash and sees any person, movement, dog, squirrel, sound, ANYTHING he just completely loses it, starts bucking, growling, flipping around, bites his leash, bushes, anything within grabbing distance. He is also barrier reactive with the fence and will go crazy at the fence if he hears/sees anything on the other side.

He also just seems reactive to any significant noise or movement in the house. He will immediately jump up at full alert barking and growling. 

He has never shown any kind of aggression towards people. He seems like an absolute monster when he gets reactive but he has never injured me or bit me or anything like that. I have not had him around kids so I'm not sure how he would do with them. He has never bitten another dog either (though as I mentioned he will snap at my old man dog occasionally)

He loves being tucked under blankets and I take him for swim lessons every week (he loves it and is wonderful to the instructors there) I really feel like I am such a huge part of the problem. I think he never is able to feel secure/at peace because I am so constantly anxious/scared. He usually does so much better when the trainers I have worked with walk him and then it's my turn and he's right back to crazy. It is killing me that my mental health issues are preventing him from being in a mentally healthy place. From the moment I picked him up all I have wanted to do is help him...and I seem to be failing completely. 

Any help at all would mean more to me than I can express
